wholeQuestion.question: An adult develops painful, purpuric skin lesions shortly after starting warfarin. Which assessment most directly addresses suspected warfarin-associated skin necrosis?
choices: Review timing after initiation, protein C or S deficiency, dose and overlap history, skin pain or discoloration, and thrombosis.
Review VTE date, parenteral start, warfarin start, INR sequence, bleeding, platelets, kidney function, adherence, and discharge access.
Review greens, oils, nutrition shakes, enteral feeds, supplements, appetite, weight loss, diarrhea, alcohol, and INR trend.
Review hemodynamics, site, INR, hemoglobin, platelets, fibrinogen, last dose, indication, thrombosis risk, imaging, and procedural control.
wholeQuestion.rationale: Early reduction of protein C before slower procoagulant factors are fully reduced can contribute to a transient prothrombotic state. Protein C or S deficiency and initiation history are relevant to suspected skin necrosis. These lesions require urgent clinical assessment; labeling calls for discontinuing warfarin if necrosis occurs and considering alternative anticoagulation when needed.

choiceReview.text: Review timing after initiation, protein C or S deficiency, dose and overlap history, skin pain or discoloration, and thrombosis.
choiceReview.assessment: The key targets early initiation, deficiency and characteristic lesions; labeling supports necrosis assessment.

choiceReview.text: Review VTE date, parenteral start, warfarin start, INR sequence, bleeding, platelets, kidney function, adherence, and discharge access.
choiceReview.assessment: Routine VTE overlap and discharge review is relevant in VTE care but omits the targeted skin findings and deficiency assessment.

choiceReview.text: Review greens, oils, nutrition shakes, enteral feeds, supplements, appetite, weight loss, diarrhea, alcohol, and INR trend.
choiceReview.assessment: Diet and INR review addresses variation in anticoagulation rather than the suspected necrosis mechanism.

choiceReview.text: Review hemodynamics, site, INR, hemoglobin, platelets, fibrinogen, last dose, indication, thrombosis risk, imaging, and procedural control.
choiceReview.assessment: Bleeding and source-control assessment does not directly address the characteristic initiation-associated skin syndrome.

wholeQuestion.question: An adult with acute heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) has recently received warfarin. Which reassessment most directly addresses this dangerous initiation setting?
choices: Review 4Ts probability, platelets, thrombosis, skin findings, INR, warfarin exposure, kidney and liver function, bleeding, and alternative agent.
Review greens, oils, nutrition shakes, enteral feeds, supplements, appetite, weight loss, diarrhea, alcohol, and INR trend.
Review hemodynamics, site, INR, hemoglobin, platelets, fibrinogen, last dose, indication, thrombosis risk, imaging, and procedural control.
Review CYP2C9 and VKORC1 results, tested alleles, ancestry, age, interacting drugs, liver function, nutrition, indication, initial dose, and INR trajectory.
wholeQuestion.rationale: Warfarin initiation during acute HIT can worsen thrombosis through early protein C depletion. Warfarin should not be initiated before platelet recovery; acute HIT requires an appropriate non-heparin anticoagulation plan. Review the probability and severity of HIT, platelet recovery, thrombosis, recent warfarin exposure, organ function and bleeding when selecting and reassessing that plan.

choiceReview.text: Review 4Ts probability, platelets, thrombosis, skin findings, INR, warfarin exposure, kidney and liver function, bleeding, and alternative agent.
choiceReview.assessment: The key includes HIT probability, platelets, thrombosis, exposure, organ function and an alternative agent.

choiceReview.text: Review greens, oils, nutrition shakes, enteral feeds, supplements, appetite, weight loss, diarrhea, alcohol, and INR trend.
choiceReview.assessment: Nutrition and INR review does not address acute HIT and the need for non-heparin therapy.

choiceReview.text: Review hemodynamics, site, INR, hemoglobin, platelets, fibrinogen, last dose, indication, thrombosis risk, imaging, and procedural control.
choiceReview.assessment: Bleeding assessment alone omits HIT probability, platelet recovery and alternative anticoagulation.

choiceReview.text: Review CYP2C9 and VKORC1 results, tested alleles, ancestry, age, interacting drugs, liver function, nutrition, indication, initial dose, and INR trajectory.
choiceReview.assessment: Genotype-guided dose planning cannot resolve the acute HIT contraindication to initiation.

wholeQuestion.question: An adult has CYP2C9 and VKORC1 results already available before starting warfarin. Which assessment most directly integrates these results into dose planning?
choices: Review CYP2C9 and VKORC1 results, tested alleles, ancestry, age, interacting drugs, liver function, nutrition, indication, initial dose, and INR trajectory.
Review indication, start date, INR, overlap duration, factor-turnover timing, thrombosis status, bleeding, and adherence.
Review VTE date, parenteral start, warfarin start, INR sequence, bleeding, platelets, kidney function, adherence, and discharge access.
Review greens, oils, nutrition shakes, enteral feeds, supplements, appetite, weight loss, diarrhea, alcohol, and INR trend.
wholeQuestion.rationale: CYP2C9 variants can affect warfarin clearance, while VKORC1 variation can affect dose sensitivity. Interpret the tested alleles and ancestry-related coverage with clinical factors and serial INR measurements. Available genotype results do not replace INR-guided management, guarantee better outcomes, or by themselves establish a need for routine genetic testing.

choiceReview.text: Review CYP2C9 and VKORC1 results, tested alleles, ancestry, age, interacting drugs, liver function, nutrition, indication, initial dose, and INR trajectory.
choiceReview.assessment: The key integrates the available results with tested alleles, ancestry coverage, clinical variables and INR trajectory.

choiceReview.text: Review indication, start date, INR, overlap duration, factor-turnover timing, thrombosis status, bleeding, and adherence.
choiceReview.assessment: General initiation and factor turnover do not interpret available CYP2C9 and VKORC1 results.

choiceReview.text: Review VTE date, parenteral start, warfarin start, INR sequence, bleeding, platelets, kidney function, adherence, and discharge access.
choiceReview.assessment: VTE overlap and access review does not integrate these genotype results.

choiceReview.text: Review greens, oils, nutrition shakes, enteral feeds, supplements, appetite, weight loss, diarrhea, alcohol, and INR trend.
choiceReview.assessment: Nutrition and INR monitoring remain useful but do not alone interpret the available genotype.

wholeQuestion.question: An adult taking dabigatran capsules has declining kidney function before a planned procedure. Which assessment best addresses possible residual anticoagulant effect?
choices: Review creatinine clearance, P-gp drugs, last dose, dyspepsia, swallowing, storage, bleeding, and planned procedures.
Use the INR alone to quantify dabigatran effect, as for warfarin.
Open the dabigatran capsule for feeding-tube delivery without reviewing formulation-related exposure.
Choose procedure timing from the next scheduled dose alone, without reviewing the last dose or kidney function.
wholeQuestion.rationale: Dabigatran directly inhibits thrombin and is substantially cleared by the kidneys. Renal function, P-gp medicines, the last dose, bleeding and procedure timing inform assessment of residual effect. INR is not the appropriate warfarin-like measure of dabigatran activity. Capsules must be swallowed whole; opening them changes exposure. Assessment must account for the specific formulation and indication.

choiceReview.text: Review creatinine clearance, P-gp drugs, last dose, dyspepsia, swallowing, storage, bleeding, and planned procedures.
choiceReview.assessment: The key includes renal function, P-gp drugs, last dose, bleeding and procedure timing, plus capsule administration concerns.

choiceReview.text: Use the INR alone to quantify dabigatran effect, as for warfarin.
choiceReview.assessment: Incorrect: labeling specifies appropriate thrombin-sensitive assessment rather than INR as for warfarin.

choiceReview.text: Open the dabigatran capsule for feeding-tube delivery without reviewing formulation-related exposure.
choiceReview.assessment: Incorrect: capsules must remain intact; opening increases exposure.

choiceReview.text: Choose procedure timing from the next scheduled dose alone, without reviewing the last dose or kidney function.
choiceReview.assessment: Incorrect: last dose and kidney function are relevant to residual effect and procedure planning.

wholeQuestion.question: An adult taking dabigatran has life-threatening bleeding and is being assessed for urgent idarucizumab reversal. Which assessment best supports this decision and follow-up?
choices: Review last dabigatran dose, kidney function, thrombin-sensitive assays when available, bleeding or procedure urgency, thrombosis indication, and possible rebound.
Use INR alone to quantify dabigatran and decide whether urgent reversal is needed.
Assume idarucizumab reverses factor Xa inhibitors as well as dabigatran.
Prioritize capsule-storage and feeding-tube counseling while delaying assessment of life-threatening bleeding.
wholeQuestion.rationale: Idarucizumab specifically binds dabigatran and is indicated when reversal is needed for life-threatening or uncontrolled bleeding or an emergency procedure. Review exposure, kidney function, urgency and thrombin-sensitive assays when available without delaying emergency care. Anticoagulant effect can recur in some patients; reassess clinical bleeding and relevant tests, and restart appropriate anticoagulation when medically appropriate because the underlying thrombotic risk remains.

choiceReview.text: Review last dabigatran dose, kidney function, thrombin-sensitive assays when available, bleeding or procedure urgency, thrombosis indication, and possible rebound.
choiceReview.assessment: The key covers exposure, renal function, urgency, available assays, thrombotic indication and possible recurrence.

choiceReview.text: Use INR alone to quantify dabigatran and decide whether urgent reversal is needed.
choiceReview.assessment: Incorrect: INR alone is not a suitable measure for this urgent dabigatran assessment.

choiceReview.text: Assume idarucizumab reverses factor Xa inhibitors as well as dabigatran.
choiceReview.assessment: Incorrect: idarucizumab specifically binds dabigatran, not a universal factor Xa antidote.

choiceReview.text: Prioritize capsule-storage and feeding-tube counseling while delaying assessment of life-threatening bleeding.
choiceReview.assessment: Incorrect: counseling cannot take priority over assessment of life-threatening bleeding.
